statements.description: The relay creates its private state directory with mode 0700 and its database files with mode 0600.
statements.remarks: Your organization operates the relay and its host.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the messaging relay foundation from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-13). The relay carries no messages yet.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay foundation logs its start, its refusals, the requests it rejects and its stop, one JSON line each.

statements.description: The relay foundation logs the events it handles: that it is listening, a refused start with its reason, a rejected request with its route and method but never its path, a failed health check, and its stop. Every log call writes exactly one JSON line. The relay carries no messages yet, so there are no message events to log. CI tests of the built relay and of its logger prove these events.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects the events it logs at its sites, collects the relay's log lines with its own logging, and reviews them.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay closes clients that send their request too slowly.

statements.description: The relay closes slow clients: a client must send its headers within 5 seconds and its whole request within 10, and one that stops in the middle of its headers is closed after about 5 seconds. The relay carries no messages yet, so it has no message rate or size limits. CI tests of the relay's server prove these limits.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the relay's host and network against denial of service, for example with its reverse proxy's limits.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay ends a connection whose request does not arrive in time.

statements.description: The relay ends a connection whose request does not arrive in time: 5 seconds for the headers and 10 seconds for the whole request, and a client that stops in the middle of its headers is closed after about 5 seconds. CI tests of the relay's server prove these deadlines.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the idle limits of its reverse proxy and network in front of the relay.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay reads its secrets only from private files and registers each value with its redactor.

statements.description: The relay reads its secrets only from files: a secret given as a plain environment value stops it before its state directory exists, naming the variable and not the value. A secret file that group or others can read is refused with the chmod hint, and so is a link to one. Every loaded value is registered with the redactor, so text containing it shows only the secret's name. CI tests of the relay's secret loader and of the built relay prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization creates and stores the relay's secrets at its site, with files only the relay's account can read, and rotates them.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay takes no secret as a plain value, and a secret it loads appears in no output or state file.

statements.description: The relay keeps secrets out of plain configuration and static storage it writes: a secret, the log pseudonym key or a tenant key given as a plain environment value stops it, naming the variable only, and a secret supplied through a file is loaded and named in the start line but its value appears in no output, state file or state entry name. CI tests of the built relay prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the relay's secrets out of the images, scripts and configuration it builds for its site.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay checks its settings and its requests and refuses what it does not expect.

statements.description: The relay checks what it is given: unknown RELAY_ settings, a malformed port and unknown arguments stop it at start, and its server answers only GET /healthz, giving 405 for another method and 404 for any other path without echoing the path or the query. A secret file that is empty, over 16 KiB, shorter than 8 characters or holds an inner line break is refused. CI tests of the relay prove these checks.
statements.remarks: Your organization validates what it sends to the relay from its own systems.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay's errors name the problem without its values, paths or stack traces.

statements.description: The relay's errors say what went wrong without exposing values: a refused setting is named without its value, a missing or damaged program file prints one fixed sentence with no path or stack, a rejected request is answered without echoing its path, and a refused secret file names the secret but never its content. CI tests of the built relay and of its secret loader prove these messages.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who at its site may read the relay's error output.

implemented-requirements.description: The relay starts only with settings it knows, in the form it expects, on the Node version it was built for.

statements.description: The relay refuses to start on settings it does not know or cannot read: an unknown RELAY_ variable, a malformed port and an unknown argument each stop it with exit 1 and a start-refused line that names the setting, never its value. It also refuses a Node version older than 26.13.1 with one plain sentence. CI tests of the built relay prove these refusals.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the relay's configuration at its site and keeps it under its own change control.

control-implementations.description: Supply-chain statements generated from the component inventory. Do not edit by hand: run node compliance/src/cli.ts supply-chain-statements --write.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the component inventory lists its resources.

statements.description: The component inventory (compliance/resources.json) lists these resources for Relay, each with the pin the repository uses: npm package jose 6.2.17, image gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13 nonroot@sha256:1d736cf8b5716c07a245301f92717143215d248fd55771ee1936ef4b3302e531 and image docker.io/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api 0.101@sha256:2cf09d66a86fdd210e42ee91662216364acc27da1163a8c44167a77ea3a6559a. The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when a resource the repository uses has no reviewed entry, or an entry lists a file that no longer uses it.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the inventory of what it installs at its site, with its owners, and reconciles it with this list.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: its resources are reviewed and pinned before use.

statements.description: These resources of Relay each have a reviewed register entry with their licence, compliance fit and conditions, and are pinned as the component inventory lists them: npm package jose 6.2.17, image gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13 nonroot@sha256:1d736cf8b5716c07a245301f92717143215d248fd55771ee1936ef4b3302e531 and image docker.io/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api 0.101@sha256:2cf09d66a86fdd210e42ee91662216364acc27da1163a8c44167a77ea3a6559a. The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when one of them has no reviewed entry, is marked as not fitting, or is an image without a sha256 digest or an action without a full commit SHA.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and accepts its suppliers and runs its own supply-chain risk management plan.
